title: Canonical workload file
description: Machine form of docs/simulator/interpretation-contract.md §4 — the only format the simulator ever reads. One closed type per file, zero parser case-splits: every distribution is already sampled to concrete integer-microsecond values at compile time; run time resolves only scheduling-influenced timing (contract §2). Ordering of `events` by `t`, uniqueness of task ids, FORK⇔spawn_table consistency, and channel/target resolution are linter invariants, not expressible here.

meta.description: Provenance and harness-only grading expectations. Never read by the scheduler (contract §4).

id.description: Workload id, unique across the release artifact.

derived_from.description: Source timeline at the commit it was compiled from: `<timeline-path>@<git-hex>`.

sampled.description: Compile-time sampling record: every concrete number in this file traces to its distribution via this pair (contract §1, RNG-free simulator).

expectations.description: Harness-only grading expectations (free-form; owned by the harness, not this schema).

ground_truth.description: Flat list of labeled intervals. Visible to the oracle condition and the Layer-1 grader only (contract §4).

mode.description: Segment mode label; the mode vocabulary is owned by the driver table, not this schema.

attributes.description: Mode attributes (e.g. wanted): flat scalar map.

events.description: Flat timestamped list with the closed two-op set {arrive, wake} (contract §4). Must be sorted by t (linter invariant).

time_us.description: Virtual time / duration in integer microseconds (contract §1).

task_id.description: Unique task identity within the file, pre-assigned at compile time. Distinct from `name`: names are the recognizer-facing process names and may collide by design (C6 name-collision files); ids never do (uniqueness is a linter invariant).

arrive_event.description: A task comes into existence carrying its fully resolved program. `depart` is present iff the task is segment-bound; a top-level task without `depart` is finite and ends via EXIT at an emergent time; spawned tasks never appear here — they live in spawn tables (contract §5).

name.description: Process name as the recognizer sees it (names only, no paths — scenario-catalog schema decision).

depart.description: Pinned exogenous depart time (the user closing the app). Present iff segment-bound.

spawn_table.description: Pre-sampled, ordered spawn table: one fully resolved child per entry, consumed in order by FORK (contract §5). Required iff the program contains FORK (linter invariant).

fork_cap.description: Parallelism cap for the fork/wait-for-slot loop (binding-time value, e.g. 8 for -j8). Only meaningful with spawn_table.

wake_event.description: Exogenous wake at a pinned absolute time (pre-sampled aperiodic input, e.g. keystrokes). The target task blocks on WAIT(channel) (contract §4).

spawn_entry.description: One spawn-table entry: a fully resolved child task. Ids are pre-assigned at compile time so runs stay RNG-free and traces stable.

program.description: A task's program: an ordered list of instructions over the six primitives (contract §3), fully resolved — no distributions survive compilation. A task whose program runs out without EXIT and without a pinned depart is a linter error.

oneOf.description: Burn CPU for `us` of lane time (CPU demand, not wall time; preemptible).
Voluntary relative wait: not runnable until now+us.
Absolute periodic wake at t0+k·period, drift-free; late iterations accumulate as backlog (contract §3).
Block until a WAKE (or exogenous wake event) on channel.
Make the target task runnable (waker–waiter edges).
Create the next child from the spawn table, blocking on wait-for-slot at fork_cap.

VM-internal control flow, not a seventh primitive — the DES core never sees it. `count: 'unbounded'` repeats until the task's pinned depart (segment-bound tasks only); its body carries per-task-sampled constants. Bounded per-iteration sequences are unrolled at compile time instead (contract §5: per-iteration sampling only when bounded).
